Any of the following 4th character sub- divisions is for use with categories T20- T30 to indicate the degree of burn: .0 - unspecified degree .1 - first degree (erythema) .2 - second degree (blisters, epidermal loss) .3 - third degree (full thickness, skin loss) - deep third degree (deep necrosis of underlying tissue) Additional code from V01-Y98 should be used to indicate external cause for morbidity coding.  439:                                                                                                                Diagnosis is incomplete; specify the site, cell type and behavior of cancer to complete it. If the behavior and cell type of cancer are not specified, thenthe morphology is coded as "Neoplasm, malignant, primary".; Note: The coders need to determine the site and behavior of the cancer such as malignant primary, malignant secondary (metastatic), in situ, benign, or uncertain (unknown) for the appropriate behavior and site codes. Refer to ICD-10 Vols. 1 & 3 for the Appropriate site code and Vol. 1 foradditional coding guidelines. The term "\u009ccancer"\u009d, when modified by an adjective or adjectival phrase indicating a morphological type, should be coded in the same manner as "\u009ccarcinoma"\u009d with that adjective or phrase. Thus, "\u009csquamous cell cancer"\u009d is coded in the same manner as "\u009csquamous cell carcinoma"\u009d. A more specific morphology code should be used instead of M8000 if the specific morphological variety is identified. For cancer affecting sites with laterality, additional laterality code should be used. See also note on "\u009cLaterality Code"\u009d at the beginning of Table 1.
